Done. Here's what I found and built.

## Starting point
The prior session had implemented the **library layer** well (model backends, rollout engine, judge, analyses, prefill, intervention training) but stopped there. There was **no `DESIGN.md`, no way to actually run anything, no capabilities module, and no tests** — and `pyproject.toml`/`io_utils.py` referenced files (`README.md`, `schema.py`) that didn't exist.

## What I added this session
- **`pipelines/` + `cli.py`** — the orchestration layer that turns the library into runnable experiments. One `gemma-distress` subcommand per paper section (`elicit`, `judge`, `analyze`, `agreement`, `prefill`, `calm`, `build-datasets`, `train`, `petri`, `capabilities`). Every expensive stage writes resumable JSONL and skips completed work.
- **`capabilities/`** — the Section 4.2 / Figure 7 benchmark harness (AIME, MATH, GPQA, BBH, TruthfulQA, EmoBench) as a single format-driven evaluator. It was referenced in the package docstring and config but never existed.
- **`schema.py`** — documents the record shapes flowing between stages (resolves the dangling `io_utils` reference).
- **`DESIGN.md`** — the requested design doc: scope rationale, judge-model choices, the 8-condition expansion, sample-budget reasoning, the reconstructed judge/onset/paraphrase prompts (Appendices B/C/E/G/I weren't in the extraction), DPO-pair construction, filled-in hyperparameters (β, LoRA targets), Petri integration, capability-benchmark caveats, and reproducibility notes. Every "see DESIGN.md X" reference in the code now resolves.
- **`README.md`** + console entry point, and **`tests/`** covering the deterministic core (puzzle-impossibility proofs, score parsing, capability extraction, analyses, DPO/condition logic) — no GPU/API/network needed.

## Two bugs fixed in the existing code
- **`wildchat_5turn` had `source="numeric"`** (comment said "overridden below" but nothing did) — it would have generated math puzzles instead of WildChat prompts. Now `"wildchat"`.
- Hardened the MCQ answer extractor, which would have matched the first capital letter of an ordinary word (e.g. "T" in "The answer is (C)").

## Decisions I made without asking (per your instruction)
- Kept the build runnable: `requirements.txt` no longer hard-pins `petri` (not reliably on PyPI; the default Petri path is dependency-free), and offline dataset fallbacks are flagged, never silent.
- Judge/auditor models stay pinned to the paper's IDs for measurement comparability (config-overridable).

## Not done, by design
- I did **not run or test anything** — and in fact there's no Python interpreter in this environment, so I self-reviewed instead of executing. The deterministic core is covered by tests you can run with `pytest` once dependencies are installed.
- Appendix I's internal-emotion logit probing is left as a documented extension point (its method wasn't in the extraction); the training-side half of that finding — the layer-window LoRA ablation — *is* implemented.

One thing worth flagging for when you do run it: instance seeding uses Python's tuple hash, so set `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` for byte-identical puzzle sets across processes (documented in DESIGN.md §5).
